newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Solvay reports 8.8 percent rise in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Solvay reports 8.8 percent rise in 1996 profit.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs company Solvay SA said on Thursday group net profit including minorities was 13.6 billion Belgian francs ($399 million) in 1996, up 8.8 percent from 12.5 billion in 1995.
But excluding 2.1 billion francs in exceptional gains, net profit fell by eight percent to 11.5 billion francs.
Publishing provisional 1996 result, Solvay said ordinary pre-tax earnings per share fell by 10 percent to 1,326 francs from 1,475 francs in 1995.

The exceptional gains were due mainly to the sale of its animal health activities -- on which it expected to book a pre-tax gain of $190 million -- but there were also restructuring costs involving the closure of Austrian unit Hallein and the sale of Brazilian unit Plavinil.
Chief executive officer Daniel Janssen said he would make no forecast for earnings in 1997.
"I would not like to make any forecasts for 1997 whatsoever ....(but) I am certainly hoping that 1997 current profits will return to the 1995 level," he told a news conference.
Hopes for 1997 were in part centred on an expected continuation of a recovery for PVC and high-density poly-ethylene prices, he said.

Together with polypropylene the two products make up the plastics sector, where results dropped by more than 50 percent in 1996. The sector accounts for about 30 percent of group sales which totalled 282.7 billion francs ($8.83 billion) in 1996.

Janssen said Solvay expected its health sector -- the second most important contributor to 1996 profits -- to grow more rapidly than the rest of the group this year. "We will try and accelerate growth through acquisitions in the U.S."
Solvay will use the proceeds from the 1996 sale of its animal health business -- about 14 billion francs, or $450 million -- for investments in the health sector.

Total sales in human health products grew by 12 percent in 1996, faster than group sales which increased by three percent. U.S. sales of star compulsive disorder drug Fluvoxamine more than doubled since 1995.
Drugs account for 16 to 17 percent of group sales, Janssen said, and 60 percent of total research spending.
Final 1996 results are due on March 27. ($ = 34.07 Belgian Francs)
